title: Plus, Minus or Zero? Work Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Aarav brakes his bike, a ceiling fan spins above his desk, and he carries his books down the corridor. One force does positive work, one does negative work, and one does none. Can you match them? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn where the sign of work comes from.

A turning force arrow shows that F and d are never negative, so the sign comes only from cos theta. Then a live simulation follows Aarav's bike ride (80 kg): a 40 N push over 16 m gives +640 J, the cruise gives no work, and an 80 N brake force over 8 m gives -640 J, while the normal force and gravity do zero work the whole way. A graph tracks the work by each force, with a slow-mo replay of the braking. We state the rule step by step, compare pushing a swing with catching a ball, explain link by link why the pull on a fan blade does no work, and work out every force on a pulled box. Then the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question on a rough slope, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET.

In this video:
0:00 Three forces, three kinds of work

3:38 Worked example: every force on a box
4:13 Exam trap: is negative work backwards?
